verdicts.notes: A wins on the stated criterion: four text-labelled tabs with an unmistakable active state ("MA COTE" in blue), no "??" or placeholders anywhere, and every derived figure sitting next to "Cotes publiées 2024–2025" and "Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · source" — B's active state is a bare underline over four unlabelled icons and it lets its own player clip a row. A's craft is the weaker half: a language toggle is the loudest control in the top bar, "31,2"/"31,20" appear at two precisions in the same viewport, and the programme rows break badly on phone ("Cotes publiées 2024–2025 :" orphaning its colon over three lines) while the top card spends enormous vertical space on one number. verdicts.notes: A is the more disciplined screen — single clear H1, consistent 12px-radius fields on a 3-column grid, an honest non-dismissible caveat naming who actually holds the data ("seuls les cégeps et le BCI possèdent"), and a correctly disabled CTA with a reason line — but it wastes two enormous vertical voids (above the title, and between "Ajouter un cours" and the caveat) that are exactly where the running total should live, and its three identical "Ex : Philosophie 101" placeholders make the rows read as one repeated stub. B is functional and legible but is a stock map dump with clipped street labels, an unexplained "16577", a half-hidden card behind the hours panel, and unsourced hours in a screen whose only job is asking whether those hours are current. A wins on craft and on the caveat; it loses the one thing that would have made the win uncontested.

verdicts.notes: A is a real screen and B is a store-listing mockup, so the craft comparison is lopsided: A has one clear read order (headline, Google, divider, email, CTA), 100px+ targets and plain-language reassurance, while B wastes over half its canvas on a bezel and empty white. Neither screen shows the thing the criterion actually tests — no code field, no expired state, no visible carry-through of a destination — but A at least sits on the right step of the right flow and only mis-describes the mechanism as a link. verdicts.notes: A wins on the things that matter at arm's length: one clear question answered by one big number, a labelled context line ("Cégep de Sainte-Foy · Sciences de la nature"), sourced and dated cutoffs, and nothing clipped — but its score card is badly under-worked, with a huge dead zone around the number, a caption ("seuil") that contradicts the title, and its key action reduced to a text link. B is denser and more honest about trend shape, yet it is a chart dump: pink is spent on both section titles and data so nothing is read first, the axis label "Jan 2021" wraps into the plot, and the bottom card is amputated by the OS nav bar. Neither screen marks estimated versus confirmed with a real visual device; A only says the word "confirmée" in a heading, which is the weakest form of the distinction the screen is supposed to make unmistakable.

verdicts.notes: A actually does the job asked of it — each node in "Objectifs programme" carries the published range ("Cotes publiées 2024–2025 : 22,0–22,5"), a status word ("Au-dessus") and a stamp ("Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · source") — while B is a colour-coded habit grid with no range, status or provenance anywhere, so this is not close. verdicts.notes: A actually does the job — per-row "Modifier", a tags card that states the payoff ("Sert à faire remonter des bourses auxquelles tu pourrais être admissible. Jamais partagé ni vendu.") and a fenced delete card that spells out the loss ("Supprime définitivement ta cote, tes cibles et tes étiquettes... irréversible") — while B is a read-only social profile that meets none of it. A's craft is also cleaner: one thing per card, a real page title, chips and buttons legible at arm's length, whereas B stacks low-contrast grey body text, a ragged centred link table and a mid-URL line break. A loses points for the nav strip guillotining its own chip row, for two identical white pills where "Préparer ma rencontre" and "Se déconnecter" should not carry equal weight, and for the "(confirmée)" / "Estimation non officielle" contradiction.

verdicts.notes: B is the only screen that does the job — clear title, a plain-language scope card ("On t'écrit seulement quand une bourse que tu débloques apparaît…"), and four rows that each say what arrives and when ("jusqu'à 14 jours avant l'échéance", "un récapitulatif hebdomadaire"), with generous row heights and honest, non-jargon copy. It loses points for the header's bare "R : 31,2" and the footer/tab-bar collision, and all four switches sitting off with no saved/offline confirmation makes the persistence claim invisible. A reads first as a marketing headline rather than a screen, and its settings list — competent Material work in isolation — answers a different question entirely.
